09939e56520311d9: KUCHING, Oct 4 — Isniah Daud was tending to her kuih stall with her three daughters when a neighbour called to tell her that their riverside house near Kampung Bintawa Tengah had collapsed into the river yesterday morning.
The 42-year-old immediately left the stall, leaving her daughters to continue tending to it, and rushed home.
Her youngest daughter, 11, had initially wanted to remain at home that morning but eventually followed her mother after her father, Mohd Ismail Mostapha, insisted she go along.
“Good thing my youngest daughter was not at home. At first she wanted to stay in, but my husband insisted she should come with me, so she did,” Isniah told The Borneo Post when met.
Her husband was away doing contract work involving the opening of containers when the incident occurred.
Isniah said she had experienced an unexplained sense of unease shortly before the collapse.
“When I was tending to my kuih stall, I seemed to have a bad feeling but I can’t really explain it.
“Then, all of a sudden, the flour and some coconut water spilled. A friend of mine who also sells kuih there jokingly asked, ‘Why did you play with your flour and your coconut water?’
“About 10 minutes later, a neighbour called me about the incident. I left immediately, leaving my daughters to tend to the stall,” she said.

The family later managed to recover some certificates and important documents from the rubble, but her daughters’ identification cards could not be retrieved as they were inside a bedroom that had been submerged.
“When we checked the rubble, we saw my youngest daughter’s bed impaled by a collapsed pole of the house.
“I was thinking, what if my youngest daughter had stayed in the house today,” she said.
Isniah said the house was about 18 years old, although she had lived there for 14 years after her sister handed it over to her when she built a new house.
She said the family had been concerned about the condition of the riverside house, particularly during rainy weather.
“Since the house is at the riverside, of course it concerns me, especially when there’s rain — we can feel the house shaking.
“We did plan to renovate the house but well, didn’t manage,” she said.
The collapse also damaged a neighbouring house after debris from Isniah’s house struck two of its poles, leaving the structure unstable.
Isniah said firefighters had advised the occupants not to remain in the house.
“As for my family, for now we’re staying at my uncle’s house,” she said.
Isniah, her husband and their three daughters escaped unhurt in the incident.
Her husband later went to the police station to lodge a report, following advice from firefighters and police who attended the scene.

The incident occurred at about 9.30am, with the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department receiving a report at around 1.16pm before personnel from the Petra Jaya Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
The department said no rescue operation was conducted as the five residents – a couple and their three daughters – had managed to escape the collapsed house.

Firefighters also found that a nearby house was at risk of collapse after some of its stilts were struck by debris from the affected house, rendering the structure unstable. Its owner was subsequently advised to exercise caution. — The Borneo Post
60365dfc3b9ff830: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The final races of the Formula One season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as planned despite tensions in the Middle East, the sport’s CEO Stefano Domenicali said yesterday.

“Based on the information we have, everything is confirmed for (us to stay in) Qatar and Abu Dhabi,” Domenicali told French broadcaster Canal Plus on the sidelines of the Bahrain Grand Prix, which was relocated to the Sepang circuit in Malaysia this weekend.
Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the boss of motorsport’s premier series “confirmed the schedule for the final two Grands Prix” of the year in Qatar on November 29 and Abu Dhabi on December 6.
The Bahrain and Saudi Arabia grands prix were scrapped earlier this season due to the start of the US-led war with Iran.
Italian Domenicali insisted “that everything was in order” and that “teams and drivers were being kept informed of the situation.”
He added that 99 per cent of tickets had been sold in Abu Dhabi and that the season-ending race was generating “great excitement”.
However not all drivers want to compete in the Gulf.
Dutch four-time world champion Max Verstappen, who will start from pole position in Malaysia on Sunday, said during the week he would prefer if the season did not finish in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

“Normally I am happy to go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi, but you know, when there is a war nearby, and if some of the countries are in conflict with each other, then I think we shouldn’t go,” he told ViaPlay.
“Then, it doesn’t matter if you have a contract or not, I think. But it’s not up to me.”
One of the Plan B options discussed was moving the Emirati race to Imola in Italy. — AFP
990f5f6eced6da60: NAGOYA: Asian Games golf champion Tom Kim revealed he was inspired by a message from Tiger Woods before his sparkling final round in Nagoya.
"Just be you. Nothing more, nothing less," read the text, South Korea's gold-medal winner Kim told reporters.
It helped him conquer all the pressure and nerves as he shot a superb six-under round of 64 on Saturday to clinch the title – and an exemption from military service in South Korea.
Kim and Woods were already acquainted before they forged a friendship on the indoor league simulator golf team founded by Woods.
Asked by reporters if he had texted the 15-time major winner back, Kim said: "No, I haven't. But I think I will send him a photo of me biting my gold medal."
Kim was visibly relieved at getting over the line when he rolled home the final putt, letting out a yell and shouting, "Come on!"
He described the tension of trying to secure a gold medal as totally different to normal tournament golf.
"It's a crazy feeling," said the world number 32, who dashed across 14 time zones to play in the Asian Games after the Presidents Cup last weekend.
"I'm just glad it's over. This day was the longest day I think I've ever had in my life.
"At a tour event it is not as if you would feel tension every day from Thursday to Sunday," Kim said.
"But this week I was nervous from start to finish.
"I told myself this would be the longest week of my life. And once I had that in mind, I was able to keep my composure."
Able-bodied South Korean males are usually required to perform between 18 months and two years of military service before the age of 28.
But the Seoul government rewards Asian Games gold medals and Olympic medals of any colour with an exemption, meaning they will carry out just four weeks of light basic training instead.
The 24-year-old Kim can now keep his blossoming career on track, having already won four times on the PGA Tour.
He was downcast in Paris two years ago after letting the chance of an Olympic medal slip away on the final day.
Kim said his next target was the Los Angeles Games in 2028.
"With the Olympics being in the United States, I will feel pretty comfortable there," Kim said.
"My next goal is to win an Olympic gold medal." - AFP

e406718a4f081554: KUALA LUMPUR: Cost of living and a reduction in regional allowances following the implementation of the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA) are among the factors believed to be discouraging some medical officers from accepting postings in Sabah and Sarawak.
Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK) spokesman Dr Muhammad Yassin said some doctors were even willing to reject offers of permanent appointments if they were posted to either state.
He said permanent appointments were not offered regularly, and rejecting one could affect a doctor's career prospects.
"Many do not want to go because of the cost, especially those who are already married.
"With the SSPA system, regional allowances have been reduced, and this has become one of the considerations for doctors when they are offered postings in Sabah or Sarawak," he told Berita Harian.
It was previously reported that several hospitals in Sabah and Sarawak were facing a shortage of medical officers after allegedly having no new doctors report for permanent appointments this month.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/regional/2026/10/1545319/sabah-hospitals-face-doctor-shortage-amid-low-turnout-new-mos

The Health Ministry has not disclosed the actual number of medical officers who failed to report for duty, although social media users had raised claims of medical officers "missing" from their respective postings.
Dr Muhammad said the regional allowance was previously 12.5 per cent of a doctor's monthly salary, but under the SSPA, the payment had been incorporated into the Regional Incentive Payment.

He said this had indirectly reduced the financial appeal for doctors who had to relocate far from the peninsula, particularly those with families who faced additional costs such as accommodation and travel.
"If the Federal Government or the Sabah and Sarawak governments could provide additional incentives, they might be more willing to go there," he said.
Doctors urged to weigh options
Dr Muhammad said the issue needed attention as permanent appointments were not offered continuously to all contract doctors, with some receiving only one opportunity during their service.
He said contract doctors who failed to receive an offer of a permanent appointment or a new contract after a certain period might have to move to the private sector to continue their careers.
"After seven years, if they are not offered another appointment, they will have to move to clinics or the private sector.
"That seven-year period includes two years of housemanship, meaning they have about another five years of service," he said.
He said this meant some doctors had to carefully consider a posting, including whether the benefits offered were worth the costs and implications for their family lives.

On action against doctors who failed to report for their offered postings, Malaysian Medical Association president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan said the reasons behind their decision should first be understood.
He said taking action without addressing the root causes could result in more doctors leaving the public healthcare system, which was already facing a shortage of manpower.
"Taking action without addressing the root causes risks causing more doctors to leave the public healthcare system, which is already short of manpower," he told BH yesterday.
He said the priority now should be to ensure the postings offered were attractive enough to encourage doctors to accept them and remain in the public service.

b2f05bf0c36202f0: NEW DELHI, Oct 4 — Indian police yesterday detained dozens of youth protesters in New Delhi on the second straight day of demonstrations demanding the chief election commissioner’s resignation over alleged voter-roll irregularities.

The demonstrations have been backed by key opposition parties, including the popular Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), who say voter-roll changes give an advantage to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.
There was a heavy police presence around Jantar Mantar, a government-designated protest site in the heart of New Delhi, which remained sealed off behind police barricades.
Local media reports said more than 100 protesters demanding that Election Commission of India (ECI) chief Gyanesh Kumar step down were detained.
“Delhi Police must stop its crackdown on protesting students and activists,” CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke said in a social media post.
“Every attempt to suppress peaceful protesters will only bring more people to the streets and strengthen the march to Jantar Mantar,” Dipke added.
“Dissent is a democratic right. It cannot be crushed through intimidation or force”.
Delhi police did not comment on the reported detentions but warned that “unauthorised gatherings”, processions and demonstrations were prohibited around Jantar Mantar.
“No permission has been granted for any protest scheduled for today... nor has any prior intimation regarding any such protest been received by New Delhi District Police,” police said.
Anti-government activist Yogendra Yadav said: “If a designated protest site cannot accommodate peaceful dissent, where does democracy leave room for protest?”

People holding placards take part in a protest demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-roll irregularities in Ahmedabad on October 2, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Peaceful dissent’
A newspaper investigation by The Indian Express last month alleged impropriety during a large-scale voter-roll revision that left millions of names struck from the lists.
The Election Commission of India has rejected allegations of wrongdoing. Kumar himself has not commented.
On Friday, hundreds of protesters gathered on roads around Jantar Mantar and in Mumbai’s Shivaji Park.
The protest in Mumbai was the first major demonstration by the CJP — which began in May as a satirical online movement — since July, when their nationwide campaign helped oust the education minister.
Just as they did in July, Indian authorities reportedly cut off mobile internet services around protest areas on Friday.
In July, protesters used mobile apps to circumvent the internet ban.
One of those was Bitchat, a peer-to-peer messaging system that relies on Bluetooth to link people who are nearby into an ad-hoc network without using the internet.
US tech entrepreneur Jack Dorsey, who co-founded Twitter (now known as X) and developed Bitchat, said that New Delhi had ordered its removal from Apple’s App store.
In his post on X, Dorsey included a screenshot of a notification from Apple that said the app “includes content that is illegal in India”.
New Delhi did not immediately comment about the decision.
Opposition parties have announced plans for more protests, including a march to the election commission in New Delhi on Tuesday and “Save Democracy” rallies countrywide afterwards.
The CJP has called for a “massive mobilisation of young Indians” in New Delhi on October 10. Other opposition parties and activists have also backed the protest call. — AFP
30a35a1dfb2fa4d2: NAGOYA: The men's national rugby sevens squad will leave the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on a bittersweet note on Sunday after achieving a fifth-place finish - equalling their best-ever performance from the 2018 Indonesia games - but also rueing what could have been.
The squad achieved the result despite only training in stints, or camps, in the lead up to the tournament due to a lack of funding.
Malaysia was placed in a tough group alongside China and Hong Kong, who would go on to contest the final, as well as Uzbekistan.

Nik Safuan Ismade Nik Man's charges lost to China (33-21) and Hong Kong (48-0) but beat Uzbekistan (22-0) during the group stage, which allowed them to sneak into the quarter-finals as one of two best third-place teams from the group stage.
Malaysia would again play eventual winners Hong Kong in the quarter-finals, losing 50-0 this time as Nik opted to rest his seniors for the classification matches.
The move paid dividends as his squad notched commendable wins over expatriate-powered United Arab Emirates (33-5) and the Philippines (34-7) to secure fifth place overall.
The Aichi-Nagoya games was supposed to be Malaysia's breakthrough moment in rugby sevens at the Asian level.

In June 2020, the National Sports Council (NSC) and Malaysia Rugby (MR) launched a special programme to groom 20 men and eight women, majority of whom were under-23 players, to become medal contenders at the 2026 Asian Games.
The initiative was dubbed the 'Nagoya Programme' where the 28 players would train full-time, year round. This would allow them to be in peak fitness and sharpness ahead of major competitions.
The short-lived programme, however, became a casualty of widespread government funding cuts and was ended in January 2022.
Nik hopes that his players can once again train under a long-term programme to allow them to fulfil their true potential.
"Our preparations for the Asian Games was only moderate at best. We were only able to train together for three weeks (in Malaysia) and for one week in Japan," said Nik.
"But with close monitoring in terms of training load and recovery, we were able to optimise the performance of the athletes.
"We are, however, hoping to be given the chance to have a longer-term programme in the future which will allow Malaysia to be competitive at a higher level."
The women's squad finished eighth overall in Japan after going down to Kazakhstan (17-7) and Singapore (10-5) in their fifth-eighth place classification matches.
They had lost their group matches to Hong Kong (36-12), China (43-0) and India (26-5).
97a2568d5b10f15d: KUALA LUMPUR: MBSA Blue Pelican completed their Corporate Super Rugby (CSR) league campaign with a perfect record to set up a final against Muamalat Bullets on Oct 17.
Blue Pelican beat ATM Vanguard 27-13 for their third straight win at EV Arena Elmina in Shah Alam, earning a bonus point after scoring four tries.

c6676e11a75346c5: KUCHING, Oct 4 — A false killer whale died yesterday after becoming stranded twice along the Pueh coastline in Sematan.

Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) general manager Abang Arabi Abang Aimran said the adult female marine mammal was initially rescued and released back into the sea with assistance from the Lundu/Sematan District Civil Defence Force, Royal Malaysia Police and members of the public.
“However, at about 9am, SFC received information from local fishermen that the marine mammal had stranded again near the Pueh Youth Camp Beach area.
“The animal was found in a weak condition and eventually died at about 2pm,” he said in a statement.

Abang Arabi, who is also SFC Sarawak Wildlife controller, said based on its external morphology and number of teeth, the marine mammal was identified as a false killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens), measuring 3.85 metres in length with a body girth of 1.77 metres.
He said SFC subsequently carried out standard operating procedures for stranded marine animals and conducted a necropsy on the carcass.
The examination found shark bite marks on the animal, while its stomach contained very little material mixed with sand.
“This indicates that the animal may not have been able to obtain sufficient food before becoming stranded,” he said.

Based on the necropsy findings, Abang Arabi said the animal’s death was believed to be linked to complications arising from the stranding, including possible circulatory failure caused by heat stress or heat stroke.
Nine SFC personnel, assisted by six residents of Kampung Pueh, were involved in the operation.
Biometric specimens were also collected for SFC’s DNA database for future reference.
Abang Arabi said all marine mammal species, including dolphins, whales and dugongs, are classified as Totally Protected Animals under the Wildlife Protection Ordinance 1998.
He urged members of the public not to handle stranded, injured or dead wildlife themselves, but to immediately report such cases to SFC through its hotline or the nearest SFC Kuching Regional Office.
“This will enable appropriate rescue, examination and management measures to be carried out,” he said.
Abang Arabi added that a false killer whale had previously been recorded as stranded on a beach in Miri in 2013.
He also expressed appreciation to the agencies, local community and members of the public who assisted during the incident. — The Borneo Post
7873a84adfdea3fc: RIYADH, Oct 4 — Flames and smoke were seen rising from a facility belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco south of the kingdom’s capital Riyadh yesterday, an AFP journalist said.

The circumstances remained unclear but in recent weeks Aramco, majority-owned by the Saudi state, has come under attack from the Houthi group targeting the kingdom as part of the war in Yemen where Riyadh is backing the internationally recognised government.

The journalist reported seeing fire engines attempting to extinguish a blaze at the energy giant’s Riyadh refinery, located south of the capital, while ambulances and police vehicles were stationed near the facility.
Both the Houthis and Saudi authorities had yet to comment on the incident.
Aramco remains the flagship company of the Saudi economy and one of the largest firms in the world by market capitalisation.
Last month, the Houthis said that they launched strikes targeting “sensitive sites” in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in the kingdom’s port city of Yanbu.
In August they also targeted an airport and a facility belonging to Aramco in Saudi Arabia’s southern Najran region.

In July, the Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, hitting Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and raising questions about Riyadh’s continued ability to deliver vast quantities of crude to international markets.
Yemen, one of the world’s poorest nations, has been embroiled in more than a decade of civil war.
Yesterday, loud explosions were heard in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa, AFP correspondents in the city said, while the Houthis reported airstrikes in the area by Saudi-backed government forces. — AFP
aeb76a4b008e1329: NAGOYA: National field hockey team captain Marhan Jalil is confident Malaysia can still qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics but admits the squad will have to improve in a number of areas.
Malaysia missed out on the opportunity to secure an early ticket to LA 2028 after suffering a heavy 5-1 defeat to defending champions India in the final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sunday.
Marhan said he was pleased to see improvements from the squad that competed at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium.
"Of course we feel sad that we did not perform in the final. India gave a very good performance and they won the gold medal," said Marhan.
"Compared to three months ago, we were able to apply ourselves better on the pitch.
"We beat Pakistan, we beat South Korea. We were only unable to beat India in the final.
"We have to apply ourselves better in crucial matches. We cannot expect one or two individuals to do the job for us, all the players on the pitch have to work together cohesively."
Marhan remains optimistic Malaysia can still make the cut for LA 2028.
"We will go through the Olympic qualifiers and I hope the players will continue working hard. I believe we will be capable of qualifying," he added.
"The coaches will identify what areas we need to improve on and hopefully, everything will come together for us."
The national squad's next major assignment will be the Asian Champions Trophy on Oct 27-Nov 5 in India.
32815bba5cb88455: JAKARTA: Two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.9 in magnitude struck Indonesia's Sumba Island and Aceh province respectively this morning, with tremors felt across several areas.

The country's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said the magnitude 6.1 quake struck at 5.55am local time, with its epicentre at sea, about 14 kilometres southwest of Kodi in Southwest Sumba, East Nusa Tenggara province, at a depth of 10 kilometres.
According to data published on its website, the tremors were strongly felt in West Sumba and West Manggarai, with shaking also reported in East Sumba and Manggarai.
About 42 minutes later, the agency said the magnitude 5.9 quake struck at 6.37am, with its epicentre at sea, about 68 kilometres southwest of Calang in Aceh province at a depth of 26 kilometres.
BMKG said tremors from the second quake were felt in several parts of Aceh, including Aceh Besar, Banda Aceh, West Aceh, South Aceh, Pidie Jaya, Bener Meriah, Nagan Raya and Central Aceh.
The agency advised residents in the affected areas to remain alert for possible aftershocks.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage from either earthquake. — BERNAMA
be9cdce308253f2e: PARIS, Oct 4 — Despite growing economic trouble and rising unease among ordinary Russians and the elite, President Vladimir Putin is not ready to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine, his former prime minister said yesterday.

Speaking to AFP in an interview, Mikhail Kasyanov, Russia’s prime minister from 2000 to 2004, said he believed his former boss understood he had made a mistake by invading Ukraine in 2022 but would persist with the course he had set.
“He made a mistake that he cannot bring himself to admit,” Kasyanov, 68, said in Paris. “He believed the reports from his security services that Ukraine was weak.”

The former prime minister said he was not convinced the war would end next year, adding that Putin was buoyed by high oil prices resulting from the US-Iran conflict and by disagreements between the United States and Europe over how to deal with the Kremlin on Ukraine.

“Putin is, of course, rubbing his hands with glee,” Kasyanov said. “He clearly believes he can continue the war without making any concessions. And he is convinced that he is winning a war of attrition against Ukraine.”

He warned that the coming winter could be particularly brutal for Ukraine, urging Western countries to apply “psychological pressure on the Kremlin” by closing ranks and urgently supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to protect skies from intensifying Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure.

Putin, a former KGB agent who turns 74 on Wednesday, has insisted that millions of Russians support Moscow’s war. Last month his ruling party won a record supermajority in elections that critics said were tightly controlled, with Putin portraying the vote as a show of support for the hostilities.
‘Sense of fatalism’
Kasyanov, who left Russia in 2022, lives in exile in Riga. In 2023, Moscow designated him a “foreign agent”, a term reminiscent of the Soviet-era label “enemy of the people”.
The Kremlin critic said he remained in contact with some members of Russia’s ruling elite.
“Fear reigns there — I am talking about the ruling class.
“Everyone wants the war to end. An overwhelming majority does,” he said.
“The difference lies in what kind of ending people want: some want the war to end in victory, some want it to end in Putin’s defeat, and others simply want it to stop, regardless of the outcome.”
Among ordinary Russians, Kasyanov said he saw “no grounds for a revolt”, despite mounting war casualties and rising food prices.
“Russians have lived with high inflation for the past 30 years,” he said. “They have grown accustomed to putting up with it.”
But a new wave of large-scale military mobilisations could trigger street protests, he added.

Speaking on the sidelines of a conference organised by the Paris-based association Russie-Libertes for anti-Putin exiles, Kasyanov said Russia had become “practically totalitarian” over the past few years.

“There is a sense of fatalism, hostility toward one another, and serious tension in society,” he said. “People are retreating into their own families, while negative feelings toward one another grow.”

After being dismissed by Putin, Kasyanov joined the opposition and became one of the Kremlin’s most vocal critics. Like many others, the start and duration of the war were a shock for him. Kasyanov told AFP in 2022 that the war could last about two years.
‘Calculating cynic’

After the Kremlin chief on Thursday said Russia would consider using “all types of weapons” if its exclave of Kaliningrad were attacked, Kasyanov said Western countries should not be intimidated by Putin’s sabre-rattling.
“The West’s and Europeans’ biggest mistake is that they are too afraid of Putin. He is not as strong as he appears,” Kasyanov told a packed audience in Paris.
“Putin fears the nuclear button more than many Europeans do.”
Kasyanov suggested that Putin wants foreigners to believe that “he is a psychopath” when in reality he is simply a “highly calculating cynic”.
“And he is raising the stakes in the game.”
Kasyanov said that with an increase in “hybrid attacks” Putin was provoking the West into taking measures that he could then exploit.
“He is a provocateur,” he added. “The only modus operandi he understands is the one he learned at the KGB academy. He told me that himself.”
But, Kasyanov said, he did not believe Putin was preparing for open war with Europe.
“What Putin wants is respect. He wants to force all of Europe to give it to him.” — AFP
b938568899f993b0: PARIS, Oct 4 — Vivienne Westwood creative director Andreas Kronthaler said the fashion industry was in a “precarious moment” as he unveiled his latest Spring-Summer collection for the British house at Paris Fashion Week.

Kronthaler, the Austrian widower of Vivienne Westwood who took over after her death, found inspiration from African fabrics and his own penchant for night gowns for the typically whimsical designs of his SS27 collection called “Body and Soul”.

A piece of African fabric bought at the Barbes market in Paris was one starting point, as was his decision to start wearing his night gown outside in the street during this summer’s searing heatwaves.
A model presents a creation for the Vivienne Westwood Women’s Spring/Summer 2027. — AFP pic
“I just lived my life in it, and I went on my bicycle and shopping and what not. And people really liked it,” he told AFP. “And I thought that’s nice, my life shirt.”

“Orange Is the New Black” actress Natasha Lyonne headed down the catwalk wearing an animal print jacket with nothing underneath, as former supermodel Heidi Klum and actresses Rose McGowan and Paris Jackson looked on from the front row.
Asked about the commercial environment for fashion labels, with many creative directors under pressure, Kronthaler acknowledged the generally difficult trading conditions.

“We (Vivienne Westwood) are independent, and there are good sides to this, and of course there are hard sides to this. But it’s okay,” he told AFP. “We are living in a very precarious moment because things are not so secure in fashion.”

Several top designers from Anthony Vaccarello at Saint Laurent, Pierpaolo Piccioli at Balenciaga and Chemena Kamali at Chloe have been linked to possible exits in recent news reports, although none of the labels have commented publicly.

Elsewhere on Saturday, French luxury house Hermes presented its women’s collection in the courtyard of the elite Republican Guard police unit in Paris, making the zip its leitmotif and the ultra-fine strap an accessory.
Zips were used to modulate the length of skirts, they ran across leather jackets and down a flared blue pair of trousers.
At the Hermes Women’s Spring/Summer 2027 during Paris Fashion Week.

The family-controlled maker of the famous Kelly bag, which generates nearly half of its sales from leather goods and saddlery, is also going through a rough patch, even though it is holding up better than the rest of the sector.
On July 29, the group saw its share price plunge by as much as 11 per cent during the session on the day it released its half-year results. Shares are down 39 per cent since the start of the year.
Chief womenswear designer Nadege Vanhee will present the brand’s first haute couture collection in January during Paris Couture Week.
At the same time, British designer Grace Wales Bonner will make her runway debut as artistic director of Hermes menswear. — AFP
1eb50752bd6f1190: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A moderate earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale was detected in North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 7.37am today.

The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement today, said the earthquake was centred at coordinates 4.6 degrees north and 96.3 degrees east, at a depth of 30 kilometres (km), about 59km northeast of Meulaboh, Indonesia.
“The tremors may be felt in the western states of peninsular Malaysia,” it said.
However, there is no tsunami threat to Malaysia. — Bernama

b160fd5848d00e5e: WASHINGTON, Oct 4 — Thousands of American women have taken to social media to support the alleged victim of a gang rape at an elite US university, in a case that sparked a national outcry, after a political commentator threatened to reveal her identity.

Messages of support with the hashtag #IAmJaneDoe — a pseudonym commonly used in the US legal system to protect a person’s identity — have proliferated on TikTok, X and Instagram since a man named Michael Tracey asked people to help him find the former Cornell University student in order to “evaluate her veracity.”

In a symbolic gesture, women wrote posts and made videos claiming to be the alleged victim, in a bid to make it harder to identify her and defend the right of sexual assault victims to remain anonymous.
“He is trying to expose her identity, we won’t let him,” one young woman says on TikTok in a video viewed over 4 million times. “I am Jane Doe.”
In her lawsuit, the woman says that in 2024, when she was 20, she was drugged with ketamine, assaulted and raped by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, a social club for male students.
Authorities initially declined to press charges, but the investigation was reopened Monday, with New York Governor Kathy Hochul later appointing the state’s top prosecutor to see it through.

The outrage soon spread beyond the Cornell case, fuelling a broader debate over sexual violence on US college campuses — from fraternity culture and the conditions that can enable abuse to institutional responses often criticised as inadequate.

Some US media outlets have compared the wave of online support to the #MeToo movement in 2017, when millions of women took to social media to share stories of sexual assault and harassment following revelations about Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein.
This photo taken on October 2, 2026, shows students on Libe Slope on the campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. — AFP pic
In a post earlier this week, which has been viewed almost seven million times, Tracey, who has nearly 350,000 followers on X, urged his followers to out the victim.

“Let’s see if anyone has the “balls” to name this Jane Doe so we can all evaluate her veracity, and that of her lawyers, since her lawsuit didn’t hesitate to name & shame 7 of her peers as gang-rapists,” he wrote.
He later added: “If you happen to know who this Cornell “Jane Doe” is, get in touch and I would be happy to publish her name and identifying information.”
Following the rape allegations, Cornell shut down the fraternity and temporarily suspended the students allegedly involved, several of whom were later expelled.
Local authorities said they declined to prosecute in 2024 because the complainant’s testimony did not establish a lack of consent.

In the United States, one in four female undergraduates reported forced sexual contact or sexual contact for which they could not consent, according to a 2020 study of 33 institutions by the Association of American Universities. — AFP

7906e61f87ecec7f: BEITA (Palestinian Territories), Oct 4 — Israeli soldiers yesterday backed settlers who seized Palestinian olive groves at the start of the harvest season, with injuries reported in several places across the occupied West Bank, witnesses and medics said.

818f4b8d6a96613f: LETTERS: A workplace is not truly successful simply because it produces more, earns more or achieves its targets. A truly successful workplace is one where people can return home safely and in good health at the end of every working day.
Accidents can be caused by chemicals, electricity, working at heights and vehicles.
Others are less visible — fatigue, stress, excessive workloads, poor ergonomics, bullying, harassment and other psychosocial risks.
Whether we work in a factory, construction site, office, hospital, school, warehouse, plantation or government department, risks exist.
The question is not whether accidents can happen. The question is: what are we doing to prevent them?

An accident is rarely simply "an accident". Behind many incidents are unsafe conditions, inadequate training, poor supervision, fatigue, weak communication or failure to learn from previous incidents.
This is why prevention must come before reaction. We must identify hazards, assess risks and control them before someone gets hurt.
Safety inspections, risk assessments, maintenance, safe operating procedures, training, personal protective equipment and emergency preparedness are not bureaucratic requirements.
They are life-saving measures. Too often, organisations become serious about safety only after something goes wrong.
By then, someone may have suffered serious injury, permanent disability or even death.
A family may have lost its breadwinner. A business may suffer lost productivity, compensation costs, legal consequences and reputational damage.
We must therefore build a culture that prevents accidents rather than merely investigates them afterwards.
Safety cannot be left solely to the safety officer or safety and health committee.
Management must provide leadership. Supervisors must provide proper guidance. Workers must follow safe work practices and speak up when they see hazards.
Contractors and subcontractors must meet the same safety standards. Safety is a shared responsibility — but leadership must come from the top.
If management treats safety as a genuine priority, that commitment will influence the entire organisation.
We must create workplaces where workers feel safe to report hazards, near misses and unsafe practices without fear of blame or punishment.
Workplace health is not only about physical injuries. Mental health matters too.
Stress, burnout, excessive workloads, bullying, harassment and other psychosocial risks can seriously affect a person's wellbeing and performance.
Some workers may be suffering silently. We need workplaces where people can seek help without stigma or fear.
A healthy worker is not simply someone who is free from physical injury. It is someone who is physically and mentally able to work safely and effectively.
Safety should not be viewed merely as a cost. It is an investment.
Preventing accidents reduces medical and compensation costs, equipment damage, production losses and reputational harm.
More importantly, it prevents human suffering. A safe workplace can improve morale, productivity, employee retention and confidence.
Safety and productivity are not opposing goals. Safety supports sustainable productivity.
We must also take near misses seriously. A near miss is a warning — an opportunity to prevent a more serious accident.
Instead of saying, "Nothing happened," we should ask, "What could have happened, and what must we do to ensure it does not happen?"
Workers should be encouraged to report near misses and hazards. The objective should be to identify root causes and prevent recurrence, not simply to find someone to blame.
Ultimately, safety is about culture. Rules and regulations are necessary, but rules alone cannot create a safe workplace.
We need leadership, commitment and accountability. Every manager should regularly ask:
Are our workers properly trained? Are risks properly assessed and controlled? Are safety procedures actually being followed?
Can workers report hazards without fear? Are contractors meeting the required standards? And are we learning from accidents and near misses?
The workplace is also changing rapidly through automation, artificial intelligence, new technologies, flexible working arrangements and changing workforce demographics.
New technology should not merely make work faster. It should make work safer.
We must use technology to identify hazards, improve training, strengthen emergency response and reduce workers' exposure to dangerous tasks.
At the end of the day, workplace safety is about people. Behind every worker is a family. Behind every injury is a human story.
And behind every workplace fatality is a family whose life may never be the same again.
We must therefore move:
From reacting to accidents to preventing them.
From compliance to commitment.
From blame to learning.
From silence to speaking up.
And from seeing safety as a cost to recognising it as an investment in people and the future of our organisations.
Let every worker know: "My life matters. My health matters. My safety matters."
And let every employer understand: "Every accident we prevent is a life we protect."
The true measure of a successful workplace is not simply how much it produces, but how well it protects the people who make that success possible.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Safety advocate
Kuala Lumpur

a0c671e011308805: OCTOBER 4 — The increasing integration of digital technology into children’s everyday lives has generated considerable interest in its implications for psychological development, particularly emotional regulation.

Smartphones, tablets, computers, and other digital devices are now embedded in children’s educational, recreational, and social experiences. Although digital technology can provide valuable opportunities for learning, creativity, and social connection, concerns have emerged regarding the potential implications of excessive or poorly regulated screen use for children’s emotional functioning.

From a psychological perspective, however, the relationship between screen time and emotional regulation should not be conceptualised as a simple causal relationship. Rather, it is likely to reflect a complex and potentially reciprocal process shaped by developmental characteristics, the functions of screen use, parental practices, social interaction, and opportunities to develop adaptive regulatory strategies.

Emotional regulation refers to the processes through which individuals monitor, evaluate, and modify their emotional responses in accordance with situational demands and personal goals. During childhood, these capacities remain under development and are progressively shaped through repeated experiences of managing frustration, disappointment, boredom, and interpersonal conflict. Gross’s Process Model of Emotion Regulation provides a useful framework for understanding this process.

The model identifies several points at which emotions can be regulated, including situation selection, situation modification, attentional deployment, cognitive reappraisal, and response modulation. Within this framework, screen use may function as a form of attentional deployment when children use digital stimulation to distract themselves from unpleasant emotions. Although such distraction may provide immediate relief, repeated reliance on screens for emotional relief may reduce opportunities to practise other adaptive regulatory strategies.

This issue becomes particularly relevant when digital devices are routinely used to manage children’s emotional states. For example, a child who is consistently given a smartphone whenever they become bored, frustrated, or distressed may learn to associate negative emotional experiences with the immediate availability of digital stimulation. Although this approach may reduce distress in the short term, the rapid relief may reinforce its repeated use as a coping strategy. The central concern, therefore, is not necessarily screen exposure itself, but whether digital devices increasingly displace opportunities for children to learn how to tolerate, understand, and regulate difficult emotions through a range of strategies.

Bandura’s Social Learning Theory provides another perspective by highlighting observational learning and reinforcement. Children acquire behaviours not only through direct experience but also by observing significant others and identifying behaviours that appear effective or rewarding. Parents consequently represent important behavioural models. When children regularly observe adults turning to smartphones or other digital devices when experiencing stress, boredom, or frustration, they may learn that digital engagement is an appropriate way of responding to uncomfortable emotions.

Conversely, parents who demonstrate alternative coping strategies, such as communicating feelings, taking a break, engaging in physical activity, or seeking interpersonal support—provide children with models of other forms of emotional regulation. Children's screen-related behaviours should therefore be understood within the broader behavioural environment in which it develops.

Vygotsky’s Sociocultural Theory provides a complementary perspective by emphasising the role of social interaction in psychological development. According to this framework, children develop higher psychological functions through interactions with more knowledgeable others, including parents, teachers, and other significant adults. Emotional regulation is therefore not acquired exclusively through individual experience; it is also socially mediated through language, guidance, modelling, and emotional scaffolding.

Conversations in which adults help children identify emotions, interpret social situations, and consider alternative responses represent important developmental experiences. When prolonged solitary screen use replaces meaningful interpersonal interaction, children may have fewer opportunities for these emotionally supportive exchanges. The issue is therefore not simply how much screen exposure a child receives, but whether screen use displaces interactions that contribute to emotional and social development.

Attachment Theory further highlights the significance of responsive caregiving in emotional development. From an attachment-based perspective, caregivers initially function as external regulators of children’s emotional states. Through consistent, sensitive, and responsive interactions, children gradually internalise strategies for managing distress and develop increasing confidence in regulating emotions independently.

Digital devices may become problematic when they consistently substitute for interpersonal co-regulation. For instance, if a screen is routinely used to immediately pacify a distressed child rather than providing emotional reassurance and helping the child understand the source of distress, opportunities for relational regulation may be reduced. Nevertheless, screen use should not be assumed to inherently undermine attachment. Its implications depend substantially on how technology is incorporated into existing patterns of parent–child interaction.

Ultimately, the relationship between children’s screen use and emotional regulation is multidimensional. Gross’s Process Model highlights how screens may function as an external means of managing emotional states; Bandura’s Social Learning Theory illustrates how digital coping behaviours may be acquired through observation and reinforcement; Vygotsky’s Sociocultural Theory emphasises the developmental importance of interpersonal scaffolding; and Attachment Theory underscores the role of responsive relationships in the gradual development of self-regulation.

Collectively, these perspectives suggest that the central question should extend beyond “How much screen time is too much?” to ask, “What psychological function does screen time serve in the child’s emotional and developmental life?” A psychologically informed approach should therefore consider whether digital technology complements or displaces opportunities for social interaction, play, sleep, emotional communication, and the development of independent regulatory capacities.
* The author is a senior lecturer at the Faculty of Education, Universiti Malaya, and a Registered Clinical Psychologist, and can be reached at symaisarah.alwi@um.edu.my

729f8484d8a34d55: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to strengthen against the US dollar next week, trading in the range of RM4.07 to RM4.08, as weaker-than-expected US employment data could reinforce expectations that the US Federal Reserve might skip a rate hike this month.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid told Bernama that the latest US labour market data could weigh on the greenback and provide support for the ringgit.
He pointed out that US non-farm payrolls (NFP) rose by only 29,000 jobs in September, well below market expectations of 89,000, while the unemployment rate increased to 4.2 per cent.

Mohd Afzanizam said the focus next week would be on the tabling of Malaysia's Budget 2027 on Oct 9, with market participants likely to assess the government's fiscal deficit target for 2027 and whether there would be any adjustment to this year's deficit target of 3.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP).
He said the government's total revenue grew 12 per cent to RM165.4 billion in the first half of 2026, driven mainly by a 32 per cent increase in sales and service tax collection.
However, operating expenditure rose 14.4 per cent to RM94.6 billion, underpinned by a 61.2 per cent increase in subsidies to RM38.0 billion during the period, he noted.

"In this regard, market participants will be observing the macroeconomic targets, such as GDP, inflation and the fiscal deficit for 2027 given that external risks remain fairly visible next year," he added.

However, the ringgit depreciated against the British pound to 5.3927/3993 from 5.3907/3973 a week earlier and fell vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5906/5941 from 2.5764/5797 previously.

402f028f0af77e64: PETALING JAYA: Political parties are being pushed towards electoral cooperation by a lack of confidence in their strengths, but mixed signals over potential partners risk leaving voters unclear about who they are being asked to put into government, analysts said.

They warn that the same problem could become even sharper at the next general election (GE16), with no single party likely to command a majority, making alliances necessary even before parties settle how they intend to govern together.
Tawfik Yaakub of Universiti Malaya said almost every party now faces limits in terms of geographical influence, voter segments and the ability to win outright at the polls.
“Political cooperation today is not merely about ideological similarities, but also a strategy to avoid clashes between parties and vote-splitting,” he told FMT.

He said this was why parties were exploring different forms of cooperation, although the challenge was balancing electoral gains against the risk of each coalition or party losing their own identity and traditional base.
That dilemma has already become visible in Melaka, he said, with Pakatan Harapan sending conflicting signals about possible cooperation.

On Sept 29, Amanah communications director Khalid Samad said PH had no intention of working with Barisan Nasional or Perikatan Nasional, only for Melaka Amanah chief Ashraf Mukhlis Minghat to later suggest that the coalition had not closed the door on cooperation with BN or Bersatu.

BN has also kept its options open: chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi earlier said the coalition was willing to extend its cooperation with PN to Melaka, while Umno secretary-general Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki later added that BN’s doors remain open to all parties, including PH.
Bersatu, meanwhile, has said it will not enter into any pact for the Melaka polls, including with PH.

Tawfik said conflicting statements from political leaders risk creating three perceptions among voters: that parties lacked a clear direction, decisions were driven mainly by elite negotiations, and positions announced today could change tomorrow.
Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri of Global Asia Consulting said cooperation should not be treated only as a matter of seat arithmetic, as each party carries its own records and baggage.
“A party does not only carry a logo. It carries history, administrative records, leadership track records, controversies and voters’ perceptions.

“For instance, whoever cooperates with BN may benefit from its governance experience, but may also have to face questions on integrity and perceptions over institutional management that continue to plague the party,” he said.
Zaharuddin said a growing number of voters were questioning not only who their candidates were, but what post-election pact their party is likely to strike.
“Voters are increasingly asking, ‘If I vote for this party, who will they sit with after the results are announced?’” he said.
Seat arithmetic may decide who has enough numbers to form a government, Zaharuddin said, but not how it governs.
The challenge after GE16, Tawfik said, would be whether parties could move beyond a “coalition of numbers” to a “coalition of purpose”.

Both analysts said disputes could emerge after a government is formed, especially over the distribution of posts, economic policy, identity issues, federal-state relations and matters central to each party’s identity.
For voters, they said the issue was no longer only who wins in Melaka, but whether parties can explain why they are joining forces, with whom, and what kind of government that would produce.
8f9a3ce7035cb66e: PETALING JAYA: Parti-parti politik semakin cenderung ke arah kerjasama pilihan raya kerana kurangnya keyakinan terhadap kekuatan masing-masing tetapi kenyataan bercanggah mengenai rakan kerjasama boleh menyebabkan risiko pengundi keliru siapakah yang perlu mereka sokong, kata penganalisis.

Pada 29 Sept, Pengarah Komunikasi Amanah, Khalid Samad berkata PH tidak berhasrat bekerjasama dengan Barisan Nasional (BN) atau Perikatan Nasional (PN), tetapi Ketua Amanah Melaka, Ashraf Mukhlis Minghat kemudiannya berkata gabungan itu tidak menutup pintu kepada BN atau Bersatu.

BN juga masih membuka pilihan dengan Pengerusinya Zahid Hamidi sebelum ini berkata gabungan itu bersedia melanjutkan kerjasamanya dengan PN ke Melaka, manakala Setiausaha Agung Umno, Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki kemudiannya menambah bahawa BN masih membuka pintu kepada semua parti, termasuk PH.
Sementara itu, Bersatu pula berkata parti itu tidak akan menyertai mana-mana pakatan bagi PRN Melaka, termasuk dengan PH.

Tawfik berkata kenyataan bercanggah daripada pemimpin politik berisiko mewujudkan tiga persepsi dalam kalangan pengundi: parti tidak mempunyai hala tuju yang jelas, keputusan didorong terutamanya oleh rundingan golongan elit, dan pendirian hari ini mungkin berubah esok.
Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri dari Global Asia Consulting berkata kerjasama tidak seharusnya dianggap sebagai soal kerusi semata-mata, kerana setiap parti mempunyai rekod dan beban masing-masing.
“Sebuah parti bukan sekadar membawa logo. Parti itu turut membawa sejarah, rekod pentadbiran, rekod prestasi kepimpinan, kontroversi dan persepsi pengundi.

“Sebagai contoh, mana-mana pihak yang bekerjasama dengan BN mungkin mendapat manfaat daripada pengalaman pentadbirannya, tetapi mungkin juga perlu berdepan persoalan mengenai integriti dan persepsi terhadap pengurusan institusi yang terus membelenggu parti itu,” katanya.
Zaharuddin berkata semakin ramai pengundi mempersoalkan bukan sahaja siapa calon mereka, tetapi juga pakatan yang mungkin dijalin parti mereka selepas pilihan raya.
“Pengundi semakin kerap bertanya, ‘Jika saya mengundi parti ini, dengan siapa mereka akan duduk bersama selepas keputusan diumumkan?’” katanya.
Zaharuddin berkata pengiraan kerusi mungkin menentukan pihak yang mempunyai jumlah sokongan mencukupi untuk membentuk kerajaan, tetapi bukan cara kerajaan itu ditadbir.
Tawfik berkata cabaran selepas PRU16 adalah sama ada parti-parti mampu bergerak melangkaui 'gabungan berdasarkan angka' kepada 'gabungan berasaskan tujuan'.

Kedua-dua penganalisis berkata pertikaian boleh timbul selepas kerajaan dibentuk, khususnya berhubung pembahagian jawatan, dasar ekonomi, isu identiti, hubungan persekutuan-negeri dan perkara yang menjadi teras identiti setiap parti.

Bagi pengundi, kata mereka, isu itu bukan lagi sekadar siapa yang menang di Melaka, tetapi sama ada parti mampu menjelaskan mengapa mereka bergabung, dengan siapa mereka bekerjasama dan jenis kerajaan yang bakal dibentuk hasil kerjasama itu.

e998983e53fe0a41: SIBU, Oct 4 — A husband and wife were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a four-wheel-drive (4WD) pickup truck near the Pulau Dudong Roundabout along Jalan Dudong here yesterday afternoon.
The collision left the car badly damaged, while the pickup truck overturned and came to rest on its side against the car.

Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) Zone 4 Sibu chief Andy Alie said the incident was reported at about 4.15pm, with firefighters from Sibu Jaya Fire and Rescue Station arriving at the scene at 4.22pm.
He said the two victims in the car were found trapped and unconscious inside the vehicle.
“Firefighters used rescue tools and a stretcher to extricate both victims from the vehicle.
“Paramedics from Sibu Hospital later confirmed that both victims had succumbed to their injuries,” he said.
The driver was identified as Julaihi Raduan, 52, and his wife, Marliza Salleh, 49.
Andy said the five occupants of the pickup truck – two adults and three children – sustained minor injuries and received initial treatment from paramedics at the scene.
He said the two vehicles were believed to have collided head-on, although the exact circumstances of the crash remained under investigation.
The bodies of the two victims were later handed over to police for further action.
Six firefighters and one Fire Rescue Tender from Sibu Jaya Bomba Station were involved in the operation.
Meanwhile, Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad, when contacted, confirmed the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — The Borneo Post
25216fa1eba899a2: SANAA, Oct 4 — Yemen’s Houthis claimed an attack on an oil facility near the Saudi capital yesterday, where an AFP journalist saw flames and smoke, and accused the Gulf kingdom of striking Sanaa dozens of times.
The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive last month.

Houthi-affiliated channel Al-Masirah TV reported that “Saudi enemy aircraft” hit Sanaa with 26 strikes, after earlier reporting “Saudi aggression” against the Yemeni capital, without providing details on the targets or casualties.
Two correspondents in Sanaa reported hearing loud explosions and seeing warplanes firing missiles at the city.
In neighbouring Saudi Arabia, flames and smoke were seen rising on Saturday afternoon from an Aramco facility south of Riyadh, an AFP journalist said.

While the Saudi authorities are yet to comment, late yesterday, the Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted an oil facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, adding that they sparked fires at the targeted sites.

The AFP journalist reported seeing firefighters attempting to extinguish a blaze at Aramco’s Riyadh refinery, located south of the capital, while ambulances and police vehicles were stationed near the facility.
The Houthis’ Al-Masirah channel earlier on Saturday also reported missile strikes on the telecommunications network in Yemen’s northwestern governorate of Saada, one of the group’s strongholds.
It comes after the Houthis said that Saudi Arabia bombed the Yemeni capital itself on Thursday night for the first time since renewed fighting broke out between the two sides in July.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This photo shows a general view of Saudi oil giant Aramco’s Riyadh refinery, south of Riyadh on October 3, 2026. — AFP pic
Hunger warning

After several years of calm, Yemen was plunged back into civil war that month, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis, who control most of northwest Yemen including Sanaa, against Yemen’s internationally recognised government.
The government, based in the city of Aden, controls much of the country’s south and east—a region that is larger but much less populated.
Hostilities were reignited after four years of a fragile truce when Iran sent a plane to Sanaa carrying a Houthi delegation.
The flight did not seek authorisation from Saudi Arabia, contravening a practice in place for a decade.
Riyadh retaliated with strikes on Sanaa airport, and in response the Houthis attacked Saudi territory for the first time since 2022.
Since then, fighting has intensified with the Houthis launching a lightning offensive in which they seized control of coastal regions along the Bab al-Mandab strait.
They have also struck multiple Saudi targets including oil infrastructure and the capital Riyadh while also announcing a naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea.

The renewed fighting has worsened the already appalling humanitarian conditions in Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, with the World Food Programme warning on Friday that three-quarters of the population was unable to meet its basic food needs.
Battle for Taiz
Fighting in recent days has centred on Taiz, where dozens of combatants were reported killed on Friday by sources on both sides.
The Houthis reported 55 of their fighters had been killed while government sources told AFP that 26 troops had died.
The battle for Taiz is taking place on several fronts, including highlands overlooking coastal areas recently seized by the Houthis.
While the Houthis have conquered swathes of territory, they have yet to take control of Taiz city, which is Yemen’s third-largest after Sanaa and Aden.
The Houthis also on Friday said Saudi Arabia had launched 94 strikes against areas under their control in the past 24 hours.
Saudi authorities meanwhile reported a Houthi projectile had damaged a school in the city of Najran near the Yemen border.
Riyadh has reportedly requested help from the United States, a call so far rebuffed by US President Donald Trump.
On Saturday US media outlet Axios reported that top cabinet members in the Trump administration met the day before to discuss Yemen as well as the Iran conflict, citing three US officials.
The meeting was not officially announced. — AFP
c92b17d352357369: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The family of 16-year-old Yap Shing Xuen, who was fatally stabbed at a Bandar Utama secondary school last year, has claimed in a lawsuit that breaches of duty of care by the assailant’s parents, school authorities and government agencies contributed to her death.
In the lawsuit filed in the High Court on October 1, Wong Lee Ping and Yap’s sister, Shing Tong, were named as the plaintiffs, with 18 respondents named in the suit.

Among those named are the boy’s parents, the boy himself, and several school authorities, including his homeroom teacher, the school principal, and teachers responsible for counselling and student affairs.

The family also named officers from the Petaling Utama district education office, the Selangor education department director, the director-general of education, the education minister, the registrar general of educational institutions and teachers, the director-general of health, the health minister, the women, family and community Development minister and the government of Malaysia.

Wong, who is also suing as the estate administrator and in her own right, is seeking special damages totalling RM120,602 for Shing Xuen’s funeral expenses from the named defendants jointly and separately.
She is also separately seeking general damages to be assessed by the High Court, including any other relief the court deems fit or appropriate.
In court documents sighted by Malay Mail, Wong said the killing could have been prevented if the boy’s family and the government agencies named in the suit had taken preventive measures.
“The first defendant (the boy) had been displaying mental health illness since at least 2020.
“It was reasonably foreseeable by the second and third defendants (the boy’s parents) that the boy had mental health issues and that he could pose a threat to himself and others.
“The same would apply to the fourth and ninth defendants (the school authorities) when the boy had enrolled in the school in or around 2024,” she said.

In her claim against the boy and his parents, Wong said the parents failed to exercise due care as parents and guardians, resulting in the killing, and breached their duty of care by failing to ensure that the boy received proper medical attention.

She also said it was reasonably foreseeable that the named government agencies’ failure to properly implement relevant policies could result in students with mental health conditions posing a safety risk to other students, including physical harm.
Wong said the family’s claim against the school authorities and government agencies was for negligence.
She said intervention measures could have been taken if the necessary steps had been implemented for early detection.

This would have included a more detailed assessment of the boy’s mental health condition, including a psychiatric assessment, which could have led to his removal from the school until that risk to other students’ safety was adequately addressed.
In detailing her losses, Wong said the sudden and senseless loss of Shing Xuen’s life caused her immense grief, as she had raised her as a single mother.
Since the killing, Wong said she had been unable to focus on her work, reducing her income and significantly affecting her livelihood as the family’s primary breadwinner.
As for Shing Xuen’s sister, Wong said she is currently pursuing tertiary education but has been unable to focus on her studies effectively, which affects her academic performance.

Both also said they had yet to fully come to terms with the shock and trauma caused by the killing, adding that they were not mentally prepared to speak to a healthcare professional about their pain and suffering as of the lawsuit filing date.
Lawyer Surendra Ananth, who is representing the family, said the lawsuit is currently scheduled for case management on October 29.

e8430d48726b90bc: LONDON: Casey Jarvis on Saturday moved a step closer to winning the Alfred Dunhill Championship after building a two-stroke lead heading into the final round.
Jarvis's round of seven-under par on the Old Course at St Andrews maintained his fine form at the links event.
The tournament is played over three courses – Carnoustie, Kingsbarns and St Andrews – with the latter also hosting the last round on Sunday.
Jarvis, who held a one-shot advantage overnight, opened with a superb eagle on his approach from 103 yards before picking up three birdies ahead of the turn despite the windy conditions.

Two more on the back nine, at three and five, saw him sign for a 65, to sit at 18 under, ahead of Englishman Matthew Jordan and Poland's Adrian Meronk, who shot the joint-best round of the day with a nine-under 63 at Kingsbarns.
"I just felt like I was in control of my game today," said Jarvis, who is aiming to seal a third DP World Tour win this season.
"Every golfer dreams of taking a lead, playing the Old Course on Sunday. I got goosebumps right now just standing here.
"I just can't wait for tomorrow. Even if I don't win, to be taking the lead, I am just going to enjoy it as much as I can."
Chasing his first DP World Tour win in his 183rd tournament, Jordan carded a bogey-free 66 during his third round at Kingsbarns.
Belgian Thomas Detry is at 15-under after his seven-under at St Andrews, while Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen, who made a nine-under 63 at Kingsbarns, is four shots off the lead.
3c8639a9985036b0: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 4 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has described the party’s recent electoral setbacks, including its defeat in Negeri Sembilan, as a “blessing in disguise”, saying the losses have exposed challenges faced by rival political blocs and could ultimately strengthen the party’s position.

Speaking in an interview with The Straits Times, the transport minister said DAP remained optimistic despite a series of disappointing election results and growing dissatisfaction among parts of its traditional support base.

Loke pointed to developments in Negeri Sembilan, where he argued that the new state administration had yet to resolve issues it had pledged to address after coming to power. He said the situation demonstrated that political victories did not automatically translate into effective governance.

His remarks come at a critical juncture for DAP, which has transitioned from being a long-time opposition party to a key component of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s federal administration. The party has faced pressure to balance its reform agenda with the realities of governing within a multi-party coalition.

Loke also addressed criticism surrounding his decision to resign from the Cabinet following the decision to allow former prime minister Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. While some have questioned the timing of his resignation, Loke maintained that he would leave his ministerial post once Najib fulfils the conditions attached to the arrangement, including the settlement of an outstanding RM50 million fine.
He rejected claims that the move was merely political theatre, saying the timeline had been agreed upon with Anwar when he offered his resignation.

Despite recent challenges, Loke expressed confidence that DAP could rebuild support and remain influential within the ruling coalition, arguing that cooperation and compromise would be necessary as Malaysia moves towards its next general election.
fb0ea5a3655d0a6e: GAZA CITY, Oct 4 — Israel said yesterday that it attempted to kill Hamas’s top leader in the Gaza Strip in an airstrike on an apartment that local officials said killed five people, four of them women.
The pre-dawn strike came on the anniversary according to the Jewish calendar of the October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest-ever day for Israel which retaliated with a devastating offensive in Gaza.
The Israeli military said it aimed to kill Ali al-Amoudi, describing him as the “right-hand man” of slain Hamas chief Yahya Sinwar and saying he was involved in planning the October 7 attack.
Israel said it was reviewing whether it killed or injured him.
It said it targeted him after learning that he was inside an apartment building, saying it showed that Hamas was using civilians as human shields.

“Today, al-Amoudi is the most senior Hamas figure in the Gaza Strip and is directly involved in Hamas’s terror activities and in rebuilding the organisation for war. The terrorist was struck in order to remove the threat,” a military statement said.
“Steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians, including the use of precise munitions,” the military said, adding it “regrets any harm caused to uninvolved individuals”.

Israel killed Sinwar in Gaza in October 2024, in what many Israelis saw as a major symbolic victory, although Israel has vowed to keep destroying Hamas even since a US-brokered ceasefire was declared a year ago.
Amoudi is considered Hamas’s top person in the Gaza Strip. The movement’s leader Khalil al-Hayaa lives in Qatar and has tried to manoeuvre diplomatically to Hamas’s advantage.
Hayaa agreed in July to a US plan for Hamas to give up its weapons, in what President Donald Trump hailed as a breakthrough but Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu dismissed as insincere.
Christians among dead
An official at Gaza City’s Al-Shifa hospital told AFP it received at dawn the bodies of five people and a number of injured following an airstrike in the Rimal neighbourhood.
It said the dead were two women and their daughters, as well as a man.

Mahmoud Bassal, the spokesman for the civil defence agency which operates as a rescue force under Hamas authority, said two missiles directly hit the apartment, causing a fire and damaging the building.
Two of the five victims were Christians, the hospital director said.

Mourners gathered later on Saturday at the small Greek Orthodox church of Saint Porphyrius in Gaza City for the funeral of the two women, identified as 56-year-old Maysaa Abu Daoud and her 36-year-old daughter Mary Al-Najjar.
Ihab Ayad, a relative of the women, said that they had been “minding their own business” at home when Israel carried out the strike.
“We didn’t hurl stones or fire rockets. If any child among us carries a stone, they call him a terrorist, a murderer. But they possess the most powerful arsenal and destroy everything,” he said.

Around 1,000 Christians, most of them Orthodox, live in the Palestinian territory. A larger Palestinian Christian community lives in the West Bank, although emigration has increased since the start of the war.
The Hamas-led October 7 attack killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.

The massive Israeli offensive in response has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Israeli forces have killed more than 1,440 people since the announcement of the ceasefire a year ago, according to Gaza’s health ministry.
The Israeli military has identified five deaths in its ranks over the same period, as well as the death of one civilian contractor. — AFP
05dc312e134aff1f: I can’t add much to the paeans to the late Dr Hasmah Ali from the many who knew her better. But I’d like to say a few things that reflect on the beauty of her long marriage to the indomitable ex-prime minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who is even older and currently also in poor health.

Mahathir never hid her. She was always at his side on every occasion that protocol and decorum allowed. Mahathir, one of the toughest of all men and one of the hardest of all politicians, always looked happy beside her, both often smiling that enigmatic smile that seemed to say, "we’re equals here".

The sight of a heartbroken Mahathir at her funeral was heartbreaking in itself. Even his harshest critic or political enemy could feel and empathise with his pain and loss. AlFatihah, and may I add my own condolences to her family and those who love and respect her, and may she rest in peace.

Her passing reminds me of my own parents, both of whom passed away many years ago. My parents, in the tradition of many devout Muslims, talked about death often and matter-of-factly, not in any sombre or ghoulish way, but just death as the inevitable next act that they, and soon enough all human beings, must face.

Going to meet her Maker held no fear for my mother. But she did say openly to all and perhaps even to my father himself that she wished he would pass on before her for a very simple, practical reason – that without her he would find life hard and lonely and difficult to bear, even with his children and grandchildren beside him.

Now, my father was the tough, hard man in the family. He had been a fisherman, a farmer, a shopkeeper, often a street hawker and if his tales are to be believed, also a soldier employed by the British to defend Penang against the Japanese invasion in late 1941, armed with an old rifle and two bullets.

He had a temper, too, one well known across my village. You didn’t mess with Pak ‘Ain, as my father was known. His fuse, once lit, could not be put out but would run its course no matter how much damage it did to people and things.
But my mother matched, even surpassed, the sacrifices my father made to bring up our family amidst poverty, and in my father’s case, frequent ill health.

What she said about death was not because she wished for a great last few years unburdened by matrimonial duties, but was just an expression of her care and concern for her husband, who would truly be lost without her.
She didn’t say it wishing to unburden herself of an increasingly frail man and it left unsaid her own strength and self-sacrifice that had held the family together through 55 years of marriage.

And that’s how things turned out. She passed away in 2000, three years after my father. I always knew how her strength, unspoken and unsung as it was, had helped our family survive our own slings and arrows of outrageous fortune and helped make us who we are today.

I suspect Hasmah was made of the same stern stuff as my mother, and many other mothers out there. She helped Mahathir withstand the pressures of politics while raising their family, all the while smiling serenely as if she didn’t have a care in the world.
I can only imagine Mahathir's heartbreak at losing his life partner so late in life.
Malaysians have had both Tuns in our lives for so long that we perhaps have taken their existence for granted.
I pray for strength for Mahathir during these sad times. Even the hardest and toughest of humans still needs a strong, steady partner to weather the vicissitudes of life.
Nothing is forever. Hasmah has gone to meet her Maker, and may He shower her with the rewards of having led a good life. May He also give Mahathir all the strength he needs to carry on.
