f55546c3bb378e57: PETALING JAYA: Every artiste has a different source of inspiration. For Kuala Lumpur-based singer-songwriter Ahns, it often begins with a place.
The roads he grew up around, the Malaysian weather and even the floodwater that once entered his childhood home all find their way into his music.
That is the heart of “Southeast Express”, Ahns’ 10-track debut album, to be released on Oct 16 after nearly a decade of writing and recording.

Ahns, who works as a designer, grew up moving between Gombak and Segambut, and later spent much of his adult life working in and around industrial zones. For Ahns, those places are more than settings for his songs - they are tools to express himself.
“I’m very drawn to landscapes because it allows me to show rather than tell and describe too much,” he told FMT Lifestyle.
“Many of the songs were written from the perspective of my younger self, but viewed through the eyes of the person I've become.”
A recurring theme is how deeply people’s lives can be shaped by forces beyond their control.

“Swimming”, one of three singles released ahead of the album, leans into atmospheric, indie-pop sonics that use the metaphor of tropical weather and water to capture feelings of emotional stagnation. The lyrics repeat the cycles of waiting for rain "to stop, to pour" to reflect the exhaustion of feeling stuck in a repetitive routine.
Ahns explained that the song draws on a childhood memory of growing up with his sister in Sri Kembangan, a flood-prone area.
“As kids, we would get really excited seeing a big pool of water entering the house,” he said.
Looking back, however, he realised that as children, they were unaware of the anxiety it caused the adults around them.
“That contrast is what I wanted to capture in the song. The music sounds almost apocalyptic, but the lyrics have this childlike quality.”

“Swimming” was written lyrically in 2019, and its melody completed the following year. Some songs on the album were written a decade ago and others much later, allowing the album to capture changes in the way he experienced the world.
Some material, like “Happy Mansion”, deals with heavier subjects including violence, but writing about them required him to rethink his approach to songwriting.
“I would just write it in the form of a journal, just streams of consciousness. Then I would clean it up, edit it and build a song around it,” he said.
Ahns’s music could broadly be described as alternative, with artistes such as Perfume Genius, St Vincent and Radiohead among his teenage influences.
“Over the years, I've started to resonate with artistes who are genre agnostic. They use whatever sounds serve the needs of the story they’re trying to tell, which is essentially what I do as well.”
He also created cohesion across the album by working with only guitar and ambient sounds.

As a designer, he treats music and visual art as parts of the same project. On stage, he pairs his music with self-directed footage gathered over time, offering a visual window into the world behind his songs.
At KL Fashion Week 2025, Ahns created the sound and backdrop visuals for designer Ezzati Amira’s show.
“If I had the budget to shoot music videos for all my songs, I would love to do that,” he said. This approach made one listener exclaim: “Wow, you make Malaysia look so pretty.”
“I take that as a huge compliment. There’s so much potential in translating Malaysia into art and sound. I’m excited to just keep doing that.”
Ahns will soon embark on a regional tour called the “Satellite” exchange, taking the album across five states before its release, sharing each stop with a local artiste.
Ultimately, “Southeast Express” finds meaning in the ordinary details of Malaysian life that often go unnoticed.

“Instead of always reaching out for something far and big, what if the really cool things are already happening around you or inside you? I hope that’s what people feel as well at the end of listening to the album,” Ahns said.

Kita sedang menyaksikan satu tontonan yang amat memalukan: sekumpulan bekas ketua luak—yang telah hilang kedudukan, disisihkan oleh luak dan anak waris sendiri, serta disingkirkan oleh saluran adat yang sah—tetap enggan menerima hakikat.
Laksana anjing menyalak di telaga kering, punca kuasa mereka sudah lama kering kontang, namun mereka masih meratib penuh kedegilan dan meroyan kosong ke udara.
Mari kita berterus-terang. Golongan ini bukan sekadar tersesat jalan; bahkan amat tebal muka tanpa sedikit pun segan silu.
Disingkirkan oleh anak waris dan luak sendiri, mereka masih selamba mengeluarkan kenyataan seolah-olah undang-undang adat Negeri Sembilan ini boleh dibentuk mengikut kehendak nafsu ego mereka.

Dalam aksi terbaharu mereka yang mewarnai platform media, individu-individu ini melakukan perkara yang tidak masuk akal: cuba mencabar dan merendahkan Duli Yang Maha Mulia Yang Dipertuan Besar yang sedang bersemayam.

Ia adalah sandiwara terdesak oleh pihak yang angkuh mengira kononnya dengan melontarkan kenyataan media bertalu-talu dan dokumen berjela-jela, mereka akan jadi lebih berkuasa daripada yang sepatutnya.
Tindakan mereka ini adalah penghinaan terang-terangan bukan sahaja kepada kesucian institusi Yang di-Pertuan Besar, malah kepada asas sebenar Adat Perpatih itu sendiri.
Angkara badut-badut ini, mereka yang tidak memahami Adat Perpatih mula memandang serong warisan kita seolah-olah adat membolehkan Raja Melayu itu dibuli dan dihina sesuka hati.
Ini adalah ibarat meludah ke langit terhadap tradisi berabad-abad di mana Adat berdiri sebagai tiang maruah, ketertiban, dan ketaatan mutlak kepada takhta.
Sebaliknya, berdiri teguh di pihak yang benar adalah suara adat dan pentadbiran yang sah.

Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU)—majlis adat tertinggi negeri yang mempunyai kuasa mutlak di bawah Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan—bersama pihak berkuasa undang-undang yang sah, telah berulang kali dan sebulat suara menegaskan bahawa Raja Melayu yang sedang bertakhta kekal sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar yang sah, diiktiraf, dan dilindungi oleh perlembagaan.
Ketika kelompok terbuang ini meroyan dengan surat-surat dan sandiwara murahan, DKU berdiri bagaikan benteng besi yang mempertahankan kesucian takhta dan kesinambungan pentadbiran kita.
Cuba kita cerminkan betapa peliknya logik akal mereka dengan melihat bagaimana masyarakat menguruskan hukum dan peraturan asas.
Bayangkan senario di mana seorang individu wanita berkahwin buat kali kedua sedangkan perkahwinan pertama masih sah dan terikat di sisi undang-undang.
Kemudian, mereka tiba-tiba mendakwa perkahwinan pertama itu kononnya sudah terbatal hanya kerana ia tidak mengikut selera peribadi mereka.
Akal yang sihat menuntut kita memastikan status perkahwinan pertama yang sah untuk dihormati sebelum sebarang ikatan lain boleh dipertimbangkan untuk dimeterai.
Anda tidak boleh sesuka hati melangkaui proses undang-undang dan adat, pusing cerita ke belakang sesuka hati, dan kemudian berlagak mengajar orang lain tentang Adat Perpatih.
Lagi pula, apa pula alasan mereka selepas itu? Kononnya status perkahwinan pertama itu telah "ditelan zaman dan disifatkan selesai oleh peristiwa semasa" (overtaken by event)?
Mari kita perjelaskan: perkahwinan kedua, walau sehebat mana pun pihak yang cuba mengusahakannya, tetap haram dan melanggar undang-undang selagi perkahwinan pertama itu masih wujud kukuh.
Helah anda tentang "sudah disifatkan selesai oleh peristiwa" (overtaken by event) tidak laku sama sekali di sini!

Namun, bekas-bekas ketua luak dan penyamar takhta ini masih dengan ketebalan muka yang luar biasa melipatgandakan usaha tidak bertamadun ini dengan mengeluarkan kenyataan berjela-jela serta menghantar surat terdesak kepada media dan Peguam Negara.
Kedegilan mereka cuba mewajarkan rampasan kuasa songsang ini dilakukan dengan memutarbelitkan perjanjian purba seperti Perjanjian 1898 dan mendakwa kononnya mereka dipinggirkan dalam urusan negeri.

Ini adalah usaha terdesak untuk memperalatkan sejarah demi kepentingan peribadi, memutarbelitkan dokumen silam semata-mata mahu menutup ketidakrelevanan mereka hari ini serta mengkhianati amanah suci yang pernah diletakkan di bahu mereka.
Jika mahu diungkit perjanjian purba sesuka hati untuk mengubah kuasa, kenapa hendak berhenti di situ?

Mari kita ungkit sejarah seluas-luasnya hingga ke Perang Naning dan autonomi wilayah masa lalu—jika mengikut logik songsang itu, mungkin penduduk Naning pula berhak menuntut keluar sepenuhnya atau menuntut kedaulatan mutlak daripada Melaka dan Malaysia ke atas tanah wilayah mereka sendiri?
Bukankah betapa tidak masuk akal permainan ini apabila semua orang mula memilih mana-mana sejarah purba demi memuaskan nafsu kuasa peribadi?

Lebih parah lagi, tindakan individu yang menyamar sebagai Raja dengan selamba melayangkan surat rasmi kepada Peguam Negara sebagai cubaan mengesahkan status haram yang dicetuskannya sendiri bukan sekadar sandiwara—ia adalah cabaran langsung dan terang-terangan terhadap undang-undang tertinggi negara.
Perbuatan penyamar takhta ini merupakan kesalahan penderhakaan yang jelas dan nyata di bawah Perlembagaan Persekutuan, melintasi garisan merah merobohkan institusi diraja dan ketenteraman awam.

Ramai di antara kita juga tidak menyangka bahawa entiti politik tertentu sanggup merendahkan maruah sejauh ini dalam gerakan derhaka terang-terangan terhadap Yang di-Pertuan Besar yang sedang bersemayam.
Mempermainkan kesucian institusi diraja demi kepentingan politik kepartian adalah satu pengkhianatan kepada orang Melayu dan negeri ini yang tidak dapat dimaafkan sama sekali.

Justeru, pihak penguat kuasa undang-undang Persekutuan dan negeri mesti bertindak tegas tanpa kompromi untuk menamatkan pertunjukan sirkus ini, sekali dan selamanya dengan menguatkuasakan Perlembagaan Persekutuan serta hukuman seberat-beratnya di bawah Kanun Keseksaan.
Tiada ruang untuk memberi muka atau berlembut apabila kedaulatan Raja-Raja Melayu dan keamanan negara digugat oleh dalang penyamar dan pak turut politik.
Tambahan pula, media sosial tidak boleh dibiarkan menjadi sarang pembiakan hasutan derhaka.

Kecuali pihak berkuasa mengambil tindakan keras terhadap mereka yang memberikan komen beracun dan menghina institusi diraja serta perlembagaan kita di alam maya, perbuatan biadab ini akan diraikan sebagai satu kebiasaan.
Adat Perpatih mengajar kita "biar mati anak, jangan mati adat". Tetapi adat didukung oleh undang-undang, ketertiban, dan rasa hormat.
Tutup telaga kering itu, diamkan salakan sumbang itu, dan biarkan undang-undang berat menimpa mereka yang cuba merobohkan warisan kita demi tamak haloba peribadi.
Hormati takhta, junjung adat, dan biarkan undang-undang mengambil tempatnya.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
4a9701c3a507dd79: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain and is ready to expand cooperation in various fields, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
In a post on X last night, Anwar said the cooperation would cover healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and smart manufacturing.

He said the areas were among those discussed during his meeting with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, who is visiting Malaysia in conjunction with the 2026 Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

“Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain, while Malaysian companies are ready to leverage Bahrain as a gateway to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) market, for the prosperity and well-being of the people of both countries.

“We also used the meeting to discuss efforts to strengthen Malaysia-Bahrain ties, including expediting senior officials’ consultations to activate the High-Level Joint Committee and strategically advance the bilateral agenda.

“In line with the aspirations of the Madani Economy and Bahrain Economic Vision 2030, we are committed to expanding cooperation in healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and smart manufacturing,” he said.
Anwar also expressed appreciation for the support from Bahrain and the Federation Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), which enabled the F1 race to return to Sepang for the first time since 2017.

“Appreciation also goes to Bahrain International Circuit, Sepang International Circuit and the Ministry of Youth and Sports for their close cooperation since July, enabling preparations for the race to be completed within a short period,” he said.
He expressed hope that the Bahraini delegation, all teams, drivers and visitors would enjoy a smooth and memorable race weekend. — Bernama
6106f20efa70b037: BATU PAHAT: Form Four student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, was among her school's top students and was seen as a strong candidate to score straight As in next year's Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM), said her classmate.
The classmate, who declined to be named, said Irene Sofiya was absent from an extra class yesterday, but her friends initially assumed she was unwell.
"During the extra class yesterday, she was not in class. We thought she was absent because she was not feeling well.
She added a teacher asked about Irene Sofiya, but the students did not know why she was absent.
"I only found out later that Irene Sofiya had not returned home. I did not think anything bad had happened to her," the student said when met.
The student said some female students had suspected something was wrong but did not provide further details.
Later, a teacher contacted the students individually to ask when their extra classes had started and ended after Maghrib.
"I was puzzled and asked the teacher about it. The teacher eventually told us that something 'bad' had happened at the school that day.
"I was shocked and never expected something like this to happen," the student said.
The classmate described Irene Sofiya as a focused student who was also active in school activities.
"She was one of the best students in the school and had the potential to score straight As in the SPM next year.
"She was focused on her studies and active in school activities. That is why we still cannot believe what happened to her.
"We can still picture her face and never imagined we would lose her," the student said.
In the incident at about 5.30pm yesterday, Irene Sofiya was found dead with injuries to her body, believed to have been murdered inside the hall of a secondary school in Yong Peng.
She was found by her grandmother and a friend who went to the school after realising that she had not returned home despite her extra class having ended.
Irene Sofiya was understood to have been living with her grandmother after her mother died of cancer some time ago, while her father works in Kuala Lumpur.
Blood stains were found on her body, along with bruises believed to have been caused by blows.
A broken flower pot was also found near the victim.
2de4b9bb0f3544c2: MARANG, Oct 4 — A man died after he was believed to have been bludgeoned with a hammer by his mentally ill younger brother in an incident at Kampung Tasek, near here yesterday.
The victim, Mohd Nasir Ismail, 43, the eldest of nine siblings, succumbed to severe head injuries in the attack.
The victim’s mother, Hasnah Sulong, 63, who was still in shock over the tragedy, said she was in the living room when she heard screams and the sounds of a struggle from another part of the house.
“I immediately called my husband, Ismail Ibrahim, 80, who was outside the house.
“When he came inside, he saw Nasir covered in blood with severe head injuries,” she said when met at her residence in Kampung Tasek yesterday.
Hasnah said her second child, Affendi, 42, who has a history of mental health issues, is suspected to be involved in the incident.
She added that another child, Rurazmiza, 36, sustained back injuries after being struck with the hammer while trying to stop the fight.
“Rurazmiza tried to step in to break up the fight, but she was also injured when struck,” she said.
Hasnah, a stroke survivor, said the tragedy brought back painful memories of an incident 12 years ago when her husband was stabbed by the same son.
However, that incident did not prevent the family from continuing to care for and live with him.
Marang District Police Chief Supt Saari Mohamed confirmed the incident when contacted. — Bernama
833a3eb3f842104d: BATU PAHAT, Oct 4 — Johor police have urged the public to give investigators space to conduct a thorough probe into the death of a female student at a secondary school in Yong Peng.

Johor Deputy Police Chief Datuk M. Kumar said authorities are currently investigating the incident and called on the public to refrain from making speculations that could interfere with the investigation process.
He said police are gathering information and examining all aspects of the case to determine the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.
“The investigation is still ongoing. We ask all parties to allow police to carry out their duties and avoid spreading unverified information that could affect the investigation,” he said.
The incident has attracted widespread public attention, but police have yet to disclose further details pending the outcome of investigations.
Kumar said any confirmed developments would be announced once investigations have been completed and relevant facts verified.
Police have assured that the case will be investigated comprehensively and in accordance with existing legal procedures.
ebc85a12ec2ec034: BATU PAHAT: A Form Four student who was found severely injured at a secondary school in Yong Peng here yesterday managed to raise her hand and turn towards her grandmother in what would be their final moments together.
Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, or 'Fiya' to her friends and family, was found in the school hall with severe injuries believed to have been inflicted with a hard object.
Her grandmother, Jameyah Rabani, 65, said Fiya's friend found her in a pool of blood and called for her to enter the hall.
"I ran to her... it was heartbreaking. Fiya could no longer speak, but she raised her hand and turned to look at me.
"I hugged Fiya and helped her recite the syahadah," she said when met at her home in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, today.
Jameyah said Fiya became unresponsive when she called her name several times.
She said before Fiya was found, two of her friends had gone to her house to ask whether she had returned home after they found her motorcycle inside the school compound.
"Yesterday, Fiya attended an extra class from 2pm to about 5pm.
"Her friends came to ask whether she had returned home. I told them she had not.
"I became worried and asked my daughter (Siti Nur Faeza Khyar, 45), and Fiya's friends to look for her around the school.
"We searched for some time but could not find her. Then one of her friends screamed and told me she had found Fiya covered in blood," she said.
Jameyah said she had invited Fiya to attend a wedding yesterday morning, but her granddaughter couldn't as she had an online extra class at 11am and another class at school at 2pm.
"I accept what has happened, but I am deeply saddened. We have lost her. My husband and I raised her from the age of nine after her mother died of cancer," she said.
Meanwhile, Fiya's grandfather, Khyar Abas, 69, said he never expected their conversation over breakfast that morning to be their last.
He said he and his aunt, who had come from Kluang, had waited for Fiya to go out for a meal, but she never returned from school.
"We lived together, just the three of us. She was never a source of worry and was a diligent student," he said.
df9e4f2ff8d72af8: PETALING JAYA: Several parts of Johor are experiencing unhealthy air quality this morning, with six locations recording air pollutant index (API) readings of between 142 and 155.
API readings between zero and 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous.
Batu Pahat topped the list as of 8am with a reading of 155, followed by Segamat (153), Kluang (150), Pasir Gudang (149), Larkin (148) and Tangkak (142).
Samarahan in Sarawak also recorded an "unhealthy" API reading of 152.
Fifty-seven locations nationwide recorded "moderate" API readings, and three - Sandakan, Sabah; Langkawi, Kedah; and Kangar, Perlis - had good air quality.
832e146fee8bd3c6: MADRID, (Spain): Tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other cities in Spain on Saturday to demand affordable housing, a day after lawmakers rejected relief measures for tenants.
The demonstrations extended a crisis that has gone on for more than a week, triggered by the eviction last month of a pensioner, 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, from her Madrid flat.

The defeat was another political setback for Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and has renewed questions over whether his minority government can survive until the next scheduled general election in 2027.

His government's proposed measures, which included automatic renewal of tenancy contracts and restrictions on evicting vulnerable tenants, were voted down by opposition parties on Friday in Spain's parliament.
The defeat infuriated those protesting the country's increasingly expensive housing market.
Hundreds of protesters have been occupying a tent city set up a week ago in the heart of Madrid to press for reforms.
Late on Saturday groups of far-right protesters, some of them performing Nazi salutes, tried to get to the camp but were blocked by police.
One video posted on the website of Spanish daily El Pais showed police chasing some members of the group through the streets and the newspaper also reported that officers had made three arrests.
- General strike call -
Earlier Saturday, demonstrators marched through the capital's streets. Authorities said 70,000 people participated, but the organisers put the figure at 500,000.
Smaller demonstrations took place in other cities, including Palma de Mallorca, Santander, Segovia and Toledo.
In Valencia, five people were arrested after clashes with police, local media reported.
At the Madrid protest Marcos Sainz, a librarian of 26, said he used to rent a two-bedroom apartment with friends for a total monthly rent of 900 euros ($1,000).
Today, a one-bedroom flat often costs 1,000 euros — or half the median monthly salary in the capital, he told AFP.
He would protest rental spikes "until someone dares to regulate it all as (otherwise) we'll all have to leave Madrid and that would be a shame as I am from Madrid."
"We are demanding a fundamental right," said Javier, a 31-year-old solar panel installer. "Decent housing, stability and conditions allowing us to construct a decent life project.
"I spend half of my salary on a tiny room," he added.
Valeria Racu, one of the spokespeople of the Tenants' Union organising the protest, said in a statement that the last eight days' protests had shown the effectiveness of people's power.
"Now begins real politics — politics which has always belonged to the people and which will return once and for all to the streets," she added.
She repeated her union's call for a general strike.
- Calls for early election -
Housing has for years been a top concern for Spaniards as supply falls short of demand, with rents and house prices rising as elsewhere in the European Union.
Average rents in Spain have almost doubled over the past decade, while asking prices for homes have risen by about 90 percent, according to real estate website Idealista.
Abascal's eviction catalysed long-running anger about runaway housing costs.

The pensioner was forced to leave the Madrid flat where she had lived for more than seven decades after it was acquired by an investment company that sought to increase her rent by 275 per cent, say housing campaigners.
The backlash led the property's new owners to reach a deal allowing her to return to the flat at a low rent.

The housing bills Sanchez's leftist coalition had presented to parliament were rejected after the Catalan separatist party Junts — on whose support the government relies — voted against them, arguing they lacked rigour.
Junts joined the main opposition Popular Party (PP) and the far-right Vox party in shooting down the measures.
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo on Saturday urged Sanchez to call early elections "because the country can't take any more."
Recent opinion polls have generally placed the Popular Party ahead of the Socialists. — AFP

6fa150d27a1f71f2: KUALA LUMPUR: Field checks remain the most vital tool in detecting fraudulent motor insurance claims despite advancing technology, said a loss-adjusting firm that handles over 800 cases nationwide every year.
General Adjustment Expertise Sdn Bhd investigation manager Jegatheesan Balakrishnan said each investigator handles about 65 motor cases a month.
Of these, eight to 10 cases involve false or exaggerated claims, he said.
He said 16 investigators handle the cases, comprising four who specialise in car accident investigations and 12 who handle bodily injury claims.
He said the cases included fraudulent or staged damage, ranging from simple "parked and damaged" incidents involving false police reports to complex, staged multi-vehicle collisions.

"In simple cases, motorists hit obstacles such as metal railings or trees and later lodge false reports claiming their vehicles were struck by other vehicles. After checking, we can see that the damage patterns are different," he said.
"In more complicated setups, syndicates or third parties deliberately stage accidents using pre-damaged or mechanically defective vehicles to file fraudulent claims."
Jegatheesan said some workshops had contributed to fraudulent claims by adding old, pre-existing damage, such as side or rear dents, to a single front-end collision claim.
"Sometimes a workshop will include pre-existing damage. For example, they may claim the vehicle was rear-ended by another vehicle.

"So basically, the damage should be at the rear, but sometimes they will include damage on all sides, left, right and front. In such cases, the damage is inconsistent and requires further investigation."
He said their investigators regularly visit accident scenes for a better understanding of the incidents rather than relying on photos and reports.
"Part of the job is to inspect accident sites, verify impact measurements against vehicle damage, check the surroundings, CCTV footage and interview nearby residents or business operators."

Jegatheesan, who has 20 years of industry experience, said modern vehicle technology, such as post-crash assistance systems and dashcams, provides crucial objective evidence, but artificial intelligence presents new challenges.

"AI makes evidence far easier to tamper with, including manipulated scene photographs and falsified timestamps. That is why taking statements, conducting interviews and detailed chronological cross-checking by investigators are essential."
He said safety features in newer vehicles help facilitate post-crash assistance when motorists call for roadside services.
"So from there, we can gather the information. Dashcams are also helpful because they can be used to identify accidents. This will help us in our investigations to detect any untoward incidents."
Jegatheesan said inflated costs from workshops and disputes over repair costs had drastically reduced.

This, he said, was due to Bank Negara Malaysia's centralised database under the Motor Data Research Consortium Malaysia, which standardised spare part pricing and labour hours directly from car manufacturers.

5224991f98cdfbe2: PETALING JAYA: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) and Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) have little incentive in withdrawing support for the federal government, as both states continue to benefit from Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s administration.

Last week, analyst and former politician Ong Kian Ming suggested that GPS, led by Abang Johari Openg, and GRS, helmed by Hajiji Noor, might be more open to supporting Barisan Nasional and withdrawing support for the government after the 2027 budget is tabled on Oct 9.
James Chin of the University of Tasmania told FMT that both blocs were unlikely to agree to unseat the government with only a year or so remaining in the parliamentary term.
He said this was because Anwar had provided significant federal allocations for both states, and has committed to resolving key issues under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).

“They are not going to cut him (Anwar) down as long as he plays ball with them. The only thing they want is 35% of (parliamentary) seats, but they know they cannot get it because there’s no time left in the current Parliament’s term,” he told FMT.
“Anwar has promised them that he will increase the number of seats and resolve some of the major MA63 issues.
“So, unless BN can give Sabah and Sarawak a better deal, and I doubt it very much, they won’t agree (to help bring down the government).”
Jayum Jawan of the Academy of Sciences Malaysia concurred, saying it was unlikely the two blocs would switch alliances or pull their support for Anwar’s government.
However, he said, both blocs, especially GPS, were known to change political partners whenever it suited them.
He cited the GPS-led Sarawak government’s cooperation with the Pakatan Harapan administration in 2018, followed by its support for subsequent governments led by Perikatan Nasional and BN.

“Sabah or Sarawak cannot afford to be on the opposing side of the ruling government at the federal level, because it’s practical politics. (Otherwise,) they will lose the anchor (in Putrajaya) which they also depend on for political legitimacy in their respective states,” he said.
Singapore Institute of International Affairs senior fellow Oh Ei Sun said GPS, as an offshoot of BN, could work well with the Umno-led coalition.

He said this was evident after the 2022 general election, when GPS, having initially backed PN’s bid to form the government, withdrew its support and joined BN in aligning with PH to establish the unity government.
“GRS is more of a fence-sitter as they will see which side is more conducive for them to work with in terms of gaining federal projects (for Sabah),” he said.
Oh said Anwar’s administration was working to meet the demands of the Borneo states, which explained his frequent trips to Sabah and Sarawak.

Chin acknowledged discontent in Sabah over what he described as Putrajaya’s slow progress in honouring the state’s entitlement to 40% of net federal revenue collected there, as well as its move to seek a stay of execution on a High Court order concerning the revenue.
However, he said, this was not enough to persuade GRS to back BN in withdrawing support for the unity government.

Jayum said the purportedly slow pace in honouring Sabah’s entitlement could nevertheless be used by both GRS and GPS to gain public sympathy and support while pressuring the federal government to accede to their MA63-related demands.
73d421079aa917dd: PETALING JAYA: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) dan Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) tidak ada banyak sebab untuk menarik balik sokongan terhadap kerajaan persekutuan, memandangkan kedua-dua negeri terus mendapat manfaat daripada pentadbiran Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.

Minggu lalu, bekas ahli politik dan penganalisis Ong Kian Ming mencadangkan bahawa GPS pimpinan Abang Johari Openg dan GRS yang diterajui Hajiji Noor mungkin lebih terbuka untuk menyokong BN dan menarik balik sokongan terhadap kerajaan selepas Belanjawan 2027 dibentangkan pada 9 Okt.
James Chin dari Universiti Tasmania memberitahu FMT bahawa kedua-dua blok itu berkemungkinan tidak akan bersetuju untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan dengan penggal parlimen hanya berbaki kira-kira setahun.
Katanya, hal ini kerana Anwar telah menyediakan peruntukan persekutuan yang besar untuk kedua-dua negeri dan komited untuk menyelesaikan isu-isu utama di bawah Perjanjian Malaysia 1963 (MA63).

“Mereka tidak akan menjatuhkannya (Anwar) selagi beliau bekerjasama dengan mereka. Satu-satunya perkara yang mereka mahukan ialah 35% daripada kerusi (Parlimen), tetapi mereka tahu mereka tidak boleh mendapatkannya kerana tiada masa lagi dalam penggal Parlimen ketika ini,” katanya kepada FMT.
“Anwar telah berjanji kepada bahawa beliau akan menambah jumlah kerusi dan menyelesaikan beberapa isu utama MA63.
“Jadi, melainkan BN boleh menawarkan tawaran yang lebih baik kepada Sabah dan Sarawak, dan saya sangat meraguinya, mereka tidak akan bersetuju (untuk membantu menumbangkan kerajaan),” katanya.
Jayum Jawan dari Akademi Sains Malaysia sependapat, dengan berkata bahawa kedua-dua blok itu tidak mungkin menukar pakatan atau menarik balik sokongan terhadap kerajaan Anwar.
Bagaimanapun, beliau berkata kedua-dua blok itu, khususnya GPS, diketahui sering menukar rakan politik apabila keadaan memihak kepada mereka.

Beliau memberikan contoh kerjasama kerajaan Sarawak pimpinan GPS dengan pentadbiran Pakatan Harapan (PH) pada 2018, diikuti sokongan terhadap kerajaan berikutnya yang diterajui Perikatan Nasional (PN) dan BN.

“Sabah atau Sarawak tidak mampu berada di pihak yang menentang kerajaan pemerintah di peringkat persekutuan kerana itulah realiti politik yang praktikal. (Jika tidak,) mereka akan kehilangan tonggak (di Putrajaya) yang turut mereka harapkan untuk mendapatkan legitimasi politik di negeri masing-masing,” katanya.
Felo kanan Institut Hal Ehwal Antarabangsa Singapura, Oh Ei Sun, berkata GPS boleh bekerjasama dengan baik dengan BN kerana ia adalah serpihan daripada gabungan yang diterajui Umno itu.

Katanya, perkara ini jelas selepas PRU2022, apabila GPS, yang pada mulanya menyokong PN untuk membentuk kerajaan, menarik balik sokongannya dan menyertai BN untuk menjalin kerjasama dengan PH bagi membentuk kerajaan perpaduan.
"GRS lebih cenderung berada di atas pagar kerana mereka akan melihat pihak mana yang lebih sesuai untuk mereka bekerjasama dari segi mendapatkan projek persekutuan (untuk Sabah),” katanya.
Oh berkata pentadbiran Anwar sedang berusaha memenuhi tuntutan negeri-negeri Borneo, yang menjelaskan kekerapan lawatan beliau ke Sabah dan Sarawak.

Sementara itu, Chin mengakui wujudnya rasa tidak puas hati di Sabah terhadap apa yang disifatkannya sebagai kelewatan Putrajaya dalam menunaikan hak negeri itu terhadap 40% hasil persekutuan yang dikutip di Sabah, serta langkah kerajaan memohon penangguhan pelaksanaan perintah Mahkamah Tinggi berhubung hasil tersebut.
Bagaimanapun, beliau berkata perkara itu tidak cukup untuk memujuk GRS menyokong BN dalam menarik balik sokongan terhadap kerajaan perpaduan.

Jayum berkata kelewatan yang didakwa berlaku dalam menunaikan hak Sabah itu bagaimanapun boleh digunakan oleh GRS dan GPS untuk meraih simpati serta sokongan orang ramai, sambil memberi tekanan kepada kerajaan persekutuan supaya memenuhi tuntutan mereka berkaitan MA63.
ebc9190f6a324a9a: PETALING JAYA: Dog owners already know their pets can be remarkably good at reading a room. A raised voice, a smile, the rustle of a food packet - very little seems to escape their attention.
Now scientists have found that dogs may be responding to something even subtler: the humble blink.

A recent study from the University of Parma in Italy found that dogs blinked more frequently when they watched their owners blinking, suggesting that an action usually thought of as purely physiological may also play a role in dog-human interaction.
As reported in The Guardian, the researchers tested 35 dogs of different breeds. Each dog watched short videos featuring three people: its owner, an unfamiliar man and an unfamiliar woman.
In one set of clips, the people blinked roughly once every three seconds. In another, they simply looked ahead without blinking.
The dogs were then filmed so researchers could count their own eyelid movements.

The result? Dogs blinked significantly more while watching the blinking videos than the still-gaze versions, and their response was stronger when the person on screen was their owner rather than a stranger.
While compelling, that does not mean your dog is necessarily thinking, “You blinked, so now I will, too." The researchers found no clear evidence of precise blink-for-blink synchronisation.

In other words, the dogs were not consistently blinking immediately after a human blink. Instead, the increased blinking may reflect heightened attention, automatic mimicry, or some broader social response to a familiar person.

Blinking, of course, has an important practical job - it helps lubricate the eye and clear away dust and debris. But in humans, blinking can also change depending on attention, social interaction and emotional state.
Scientists are increasingly interested in whether the same may be true for other animals.
The Parma team previously found that dogs blink more when watching videos of other dogs blinking, suggesting the behaviour may have some relevance in dog-to-dog communication as well.
Taken together, the findings raise the possibility that blinking is part of a much larger collection of subtle signals dogs use during social encounters.

One of the most interesting parts of the latest study is that familiarity appeared to matter. The dogs did not react in the same way to unfamiliar people, suggesting their response may be influenced by the social importance of the person they are watching.

That fits into a growing body of research showing just how closely dogs monitor human faces and behaviour. Another study published this year found that dogs could distinguish between some negative human facial expressions - including fear, anger and sadness - based on patterns of brain activity.

So, should you start blinking at your dog? You can certainly try - just don’t assume you have discovered a secret canine language. The researchers stress that more work is needed to understand what the extra blinking actually means.
For now, the finding offers a sweet reminder that communication between dogs and humans is not limited to commands, barks or wagging tails. It may be happening literally in the blink of an eye.
0c00c7294fb30b4e: SANAA: Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on an oil facility near the Saudi capital on Saturday, where an AFP journalist saw flames and smoke, and accused the Gulf kingdom of striking Sanaa dozens of times.
The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen's Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive last month.

Houthi-affiliated channel Al-Masirah TV reported that "Saudi enemy aircraft" hit Sanaa with 26 strikes, after earlier reporting "Saudi aggression" against the Yemeni capital, without providing details on the targets or casualties.
Two correspondents in Sanaa reported hearing loud explosions and seeing warplanes firing missiles at the city.
In neighbouring Saudi Arabia, flames and smoke were seen rising on Saturday afternoon from an Aramco facility south of Riyadh, an AFP journalist said.

While the Saudi authorities are yet to comment, late on Saturday, the Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted an oil facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, adding that they sparked fires at the targeted sites.

The AFP journalist reported seeing firefighters attempting to extinguish a blaze at Aramco's Riyadh refinery, located south of the capital, while ambulances and police vehicles were stationed near the facility.
The Houthis' Al-Masirah channel earlier on Saturday also reported missile strikes on the telecommunications network in Yemen's northwestern governorate of Saada, one of the group's strongholds.
It comes after the Houthis said that Saudi Arabia bombed the Yemeni capital itself on Thursday night for the first time since renewed fighting broke out between the two sides in July.

After several years of calm, Yemen was plunged back into civil war that month, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis, who control most of northwest Yemen including Sanaa, against Yemen's internationally recognised government.
The government, based in the city of Aden, controls much of the country's south and east -- a region that is larger but much less populated.
Hostilities were reignited after four years of a fragile truce when Iran sent a plane to Sanaa carrying a Houthi delegation.
The flight did not seek authorisation from Saudi Arabia, contravening a practice in place for a decade.
Riyadh retaliated with strikes on Sanaa airport, and in response the Houthis attacked Saudi territory for the first time since 2022.
Since then, fighting has intensified with the Houthis launching a lightning offensive in which they seized control of coastal regions along the Bab al-Mandab strait.
They have also struck multiple Saudi targets including oil infrastructure and the capital Riyadh while also announcing a naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea.

The renewed fighting has worsened the already appalling humanitarian conditions in Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, with the World Food Programme warning on Friday that three-quarters of the population was unable to meet its basic food needs.
8ed415553440398c: KUALA LUMPUR: Consumers should not be unfairly burdened due to fraudulent or manipulated motor insurance claims, the Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) said.
Fomca chief executive officer Dr T. Saravanan said the reality was that rising claims costs would eventually affect insurance premiums.
"For now, there may be regulatory controls and safeguards," he said.
"But how long can consumers continue to be protected if the underlying problems within the industry are not addressed?"
He said it was time to revamp the motor insurance claims ecosystem as the present framework clearly needed stronger checks and balances.
"Similar to efforts to reset and reform the healthcare and medical insurance ecosystem, we need a comprehensive review of the motor insurance industry, particularly the claims process."

He said Fomca's approach was not merely to receive complaints, but to help consumers understand the issue, identify the parties involved and facilitate dispute resolution where appropriate through the National Consumer Complaints Centre.
"The first step is usually to obtain the relevant documents and evidence and engage the company, insurer, workshop or other relevant party to seek clarification and an appropriate resolution."
He said there was a need to establish a neutral and independent mechanism to verify questionable or high-value claims.
"When different parties within the ecosystem have their own commercial interests, there is always a risk of conflict of interest, inflated costs or weaknesses being exploited.
"Ultimately, these additional costs may be passed back to consumers through higher premiums.
"Therefore, the responsibility cannot simply be placed on policyholders."
He said insurers must strengthen fraud detection and claims verification, while workshops, adjusters and other parties involved in fraudulent or inflated claims must also be held accountable.
Saravanan said Bank Negara Malaysia, as the regulator of the insurance industry, must take a firm lead in addressing these structural weaknesses.
"Insurance fraud should be investigated and tackled quickly, while the overall claims ecosystem should be reviewed to identify loopholes and strengthen accountability.
"This issue goes beyond motor insurance. Whether it involves motor, medical, personal or life insurance, continuously passing increasing costs back to consumers is not a sustainable solution.

"The emphasis must therefore be on reforming the system, closing loopholes, introducing stronger independent verification and taking firm action against fraud. Honest policyholders should not continually be made to pay for weaknesses and abuses within the system."
The Malaysia Consumers Movement (MCM) said policyholders should not be forced to bear the burden of higher insurance premiums based on unsubstantiated allegations of motor insurance fraud.
MCM legal adviser Mohan Sankaran said genuine policyholders who strictly abide by their policy terms should not collectively absorb industry losses attributed to unverified or merely suspected fraud.

"Consumers should not be made to bear the cost of fraud through higher premiums as a matter of course. If insurers believe a claim is fraudulent or manipulated, then that claim must be properly investigated and supported by evidence."
'STRONGER FRAUD DETECTION MUST COME FIRST'
He said the insurance industry must draw a clear line between suspected and established fraud and suspicion alone could not automatically classify a claim as fraudulent.
"Where fraud is proven, the appropriate action should be taken against the parties responsible.
"It would be unfair for genuine policyholders who have paid their premiums and complied with the terms of their policies to collectively absorb losses attributed to alleged fraud."
Mohan said insurance providers should prioritise tighter controls within their claims ecosystem and improve internal fraud detection mechanisms rather than passing financial burdens onto the public.

"The insurer's priority should therefore be stronger fraud detection, proper investigation, enforcement against offenders and tighter controls within the claims ecosystem rather than simply passing the financial burden on to consumers through higher premiums."

He added that any industry proposal seeking to justify premium hikes on the grounds of rising fraud must be backed by transparent, independently verifiable data showing the actual financial impact of proven fraudulent claims.
